title: Variable-span consolidation and runtime pad attenuation for latency-cost tradeoffs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Static bucketing and coarse padding for mixed-length requests wastes tokens and increases p95 latency. We need a runtime strategy that both reduces padding waste and aligns micro-batches to kernels that perform best for the observed sequence-length mix, while preserving prefill/ decode correctness and KV cache reuse.

Proposed approach: Variable-span consolidation (VSC) + runtime pad attenuation. VSC is a two-stage bucketing pipeline: first perform a lightweight quantile-based grouping to form coarse buckets based on recent request seqlen distribution, then split those coarse buckets using a kernel-latency model to produce final micro-batches optimized for both the preferred kernel and the expected prefill/decode pattern. Pad attenuation is an execution-time technique that records per-bucket prefix reuse probability and allows the runtime to trim trailing padding in the network/IO path (keep logical padding for correctness, but avoid materializing KV work for low-probability pads). We also introduce staggered prefill scheduling: order prefill jobs by expected KV overlap score so that requests likely to reuse the same prefix are prefilled consecutively, increasing cache hit-rate.

Key design choices and tradeoffs: We bias buckets to prefer kernel-stable sizes (sizes where GEMM/kernels are efficient) rather than minimizing byte-level padding alone. This improves p95 latency at the cost of slightly higher average padded tokens in marginal cases. Pad attenuation reduces GPU compute for padding by avoiding unnecessary KV writes for low-impact padding tokens; it requires careful validation to ensure attention correctness when using cached KV segments. Staggered prefill improves KV reuse but can increase head latency for some requests; we will control this with a latency SLO-aware scheduler that falls back to FIFO when head latency would exceed thresholds.

Compatibility: Works with current attention kernels and quantized execution paths. Requires adding small instrumentation to the kernel selection model and KV write path. Fallback modes for Dedicated and Private deployments are provided via runtime flags.

Observability: New metrics: bucket_size_histogram, pad_attn_savings, kv_reuse_rate_by_bucket, staggered_prefill_delay_ms, kernel_choice_counts, bucket_fallback_rate. Dashboards and alerts defined in the rollout plan.

Links: design doc and initial benchmark harness attached in design_docs and pr_links fields.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end VSC pipeline deployed behind runtime feature flag
pad attenuation reduces GPU KV writes for padding by >=10% on mixed-length traces without correctness regressions

No more than 2% increase in request-level output divergence on held-out prompt set
Canary rollout automation and rollback triggers implemented and exercised

VSC + pad attenuation (A100-40GB): p95_latency: 172ms (-18%), avg_token_cost: 0.88 (-12%), throughput: +9%
Observed kv_reuse_rate_by_bucket improved from 42% -> 61% with staggered prefill
Quantized run on A100-int8 shows smaller p95 wins (approx -8%) but cost savings still material (~-9%)
rollout_plan: Feature flag default OFF in prod; enable canary 5% for 24h with automated SLO checks
Canary metrics: p95 latency, tail error rate, kv_reuse_rate, pad_attn_savings, output divergence on eval prompts
If p95 or error rate regresses >2%/threshold, auto rollback and collect logs for postmortem
Expand to 25% for 48h if stable, then 100% with staged ramp and monitoring
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrectly skipping KV writes could change attention outcomes. Mitigation: strict unit tests and a validation harness that compares logits at microbatch level; guardrails to disable pad attenuation if any divergence beyond epsilon observed.
Risk: Staggered prefill may increase head latency for latency-sensitive routes. Mitigation: SLO-aware scheduler with per-route latency budget and immediate FIFO fallback.
Risk: Kernel latency model may drift for new kernels or quantized paths. Mitigation: continuous offline retraining job and warm-start baseline per release; runtime fallback to coarse bucket sizes.
